transcript.text: Bosch SMS25AW00G, came back to E:09 on the display and the dishes are washed but stone cold. Is this an expensive fix?

Regarding your question: yes, this is likely to be an expensive fix because the SMS25AW00G uses a flow-through heater integrated into the circulation pump assembly rather than a simple replaceable element. Replacing that unit requires significant labour and parts cost. The E:09 code specifically indicates a failure in the heating circuit. To confirm this is the issue, please run an intensive or 65°C programme with a normal load. At the end of that cycle, are the dishes hot and steamy, or still cold to the touch?
Tried the hot programme and the eco one, both come out cold. Water felt cold to the touch mid-cycle too.

Since both programmes resulted in stone-cold water and you have the E:09 error code, this suggests a genuine no-heat fault rather than just poor drying. On your model, the heater is integrated into the circulation pump assembly at the bottom of the machine; it is not a simple replaceable element. Because the repair involves dismantling the appliance base and replacing an electrical heating component, this must be done by a qualified engineer. I recommend contacting Bosch support or a local appliance repair technician to arrange a visit.
